questions.q: Why can a correctly time-ordered split (e.g. TimeSeriesSplit) still leak information when labels are built from forward-looking windows?
options: Because TimeSeriesSplit shuffles data internally
Because a training row just before the test set can have a label window that reaches forward into the test period, even though the row's own timestamp is earlier
Because scikit-learn always trains on the full dataset regardless of splits
Because forward-looking labels cannot be computed in Python
questions.explain: A label like 'return over the next 5 days' spans a window, not an instant. A training row positioned just before the test block can have a label window that overlaps the test span, so training on it effectively trains on test-period information.

questions.q: What exactly does PURGING remove from the training set?
options: A fixed buffer of rows immediately after the test set, regardless of their labels
Training observations whose label window overlaps the test set's time span
All rows that are more than one year old
Rows with missing values only
questions.explain: Purging specifically removes training observations whose label window reaches into (overlaps) the test set's time span — it is filtered based on where each observation's label actually resolves.

questions.q: What is the key difference between purging and embargoing?
options: They are two names for exactly the same operation

Purging removes rows based on label-window overlap with the test set (typically before it); embargoing removes a buffer of rows immediately after the test set regardless of label overlap, as protection against serial correlation and rolling-window feature leakage
Embargoing only applies to classification problems, purging only to regression
Purging happens after training; embargoing happens before training
questions.explain: Purging is based on label-window overlap and typically affects training rows before the test block. Embargoing is a separate, additional precaution: it drops a buffer of training rows right after the test block even when their labels don't overlap it, because serial correlation and rolling-window features can still leak information forward.

questions.q: Does scikit-learn provide a built-in cross-validator that performs purging and embargoing?
options: Yes, sklearn.model_selection.PurgedKFold ships with every scikit-learn release
Yes, but only as part of TimeSeriesSplit's gap parameter
No — purging and embargoing require a custom splitter, typically extending sklearn's KFold
No, and there is no known way to implement this logic in Python
questions.explain: Neither KFold nor TimeSeriesSplit knows anything about label windows. In practice, purged and embargoed cross-validation is implemented as a custom class (commonly called PurgedKFold) that extends KFold and overrides split().

questions.q: Who formalized purging and embargoing for financial machine learning, and in what work?
options: Harry Markowitz, in his original 1952 portfolio theory paper
Marcos Lopez de Prado, in "Advances in Financial Machine Learning"
The scikit-learn core development team, in their official documentation
William Sharpe, in his work on the Sharpe ratio
questions.explain: Purging and embargoing (often implemented as PurgedKFold) were formalized by Marcos Lopez de Prado in "Advances in Financial Machine Learning" (Wiley, 2018).
